domain: Political Philosophy / Law / Social Policy / Bioethics
topic_summary: Analysis of the contested category kernel 'woman' (or 'female') as read through sex-defined-by-biology versus gender-defined-by-identity frameworks. Each reading emits constraints with different membership criteria, different victim sets, and incompatible policy implications across domains including sports eligibility, violence-against-women frameworks, and sex-segregated spaces. The debate tests whether these readings can coexist within a single coherent legal/policy framework.

key_entities: U.N. Commission on the Status of Women (international policy forum; site of definitional contest)
U.S. Trump Administration / Education Secretary Linda McMahon (state actor; sex-based reading enforcement)
Alliance Defending Freedom (legal advocacy; sex-based reading litigation)
Hands Across the Aisle Coalition (bi-partisan feminist coalition; sex-based reading advocacy)
GLAAD / transgender advocacy organizations (identity-based reading advocacy)
International Olympic Committee (regulatory body; performance-advantage framework)
Caster Semenya (intersex athlete; boundary case for both readings)
Title IX of Education Amendments 1972 (U.S. federal law; contested interpretive kernel)
Stoller & Greenson 1964 / Money 1970s (historical origin of gender-identity concept)
Second-wave feminists (historical actors; sex-based category defense)
key_tensions: Cisgender female athletes vs transgender female athletes (sports eligibility; incompatible victim sets)
Violence-against-women frameworks (sex-based vs identity-based protected categories)
U.S. 2026 U.N. resolution (sex-binary definition) vs EU/Sweden opposition (gender-identity inclusion)
Intersex athletes (Semenya case) vs binary-sex sports categories (neither reading fully accommodates)

readings.commitment: Category membership determined by chromosomal/anatomical/reproductive biology; 'woman' = adult human female with XX chromosomes and female reproductive anatomy (typical case)
readings.authority_grounding: Biological science; evolutionary biology; medical taxonomy; second-wave feminist theory (sex-based oppression analysis)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set = people with female biology; excludes transgender women from sex-segregated protections; includes intersex people ambiguously; high ε in sports (performance advantage framework) and violence-against-women policy (sex-based data collection)

readings.commitment: Category membership determined by internal gender identity; 'woman' = person who identifies as a woman regardless of assigned sex at birth
readings.authority_grounding: Psychological science (Stoller/Money lineage); human rights frameworks (self-determination); transgender advocacy; U.N. gender-mainstreaming policy
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set = people who identify as women (includes transgender women); excludes sex-based protections as discriminatory; moderate ε in identity-document policy, high ε in sports eligibility and sex-segregated spaces (access rights vs exclusion rights collision)

readings.commitment: Category membership acknowledges biological sex as non-binary spectrum; 'woman' includes typical female biology plus intersex variations that do not fit male category
readings.authority_grounding: Medical science (DSD research); intersex advocacy; biological complexity literature (chromosomal/hormonal variation)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set = people with female-typical or ambiguous biology (Semenya case); challenges binary enforcement in both other readings; low ε in most policy domains (small population) but high ε in elite sports (performance-advantage boundary cases)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Biology-reading axiom: category membership is observer-independent fact determined by chromosomes/anatomy. Identity-reading axiom: category membership is self-determined internal state. No single framework can hold both as simultaneously authoritative for the same category—one must be epistemically prior.

omegas.description: Can a single legal/policy framework hold both sex-biology and gender-identity readings as simultaneously valid? Research indicates 'sex and gender are not neatly separable' but no coherent pluralist framework has emerged. If axiom contradiction is genuine, one reading must be epistemically prior—but which, and on what grounds?
omegas.source: Axiom Contradiction Declaration (§1.3-K); research quote 'rationale where both perspectives coexist...remains elusive in policy contexts'

omegas.description: Intersex_accommodation_reading classified as moderate ε based on small population (~1.7% DSD prevalence). But Semenya-type cases have disproportionate policy impact in elite sports. Is this a piton (atrophied consideration) or a mountain (biological constraint that binary frameworks cannot accommodate)?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory); classification uncertainty

omegas.description: Hands Across the Aisle Coalition represents second-wave feminists defending sex-based categories. Is this a principled defense of sex-based oppression analysis, or does it function as a snare benefiting cisgender women at transgender women's expense? Beneficiary/victim classification depends on whether sex-based oppression framework is itself a mountain or tangled_rope.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan); extraction entity 'Hands Across the Aisle Coalition'

omegas.description: Gender-identity concept originates with Stoller/Greenson 1964 and Money 1970s. Money's research involved controversial practices (David Reimer case). Does this origin delegitimize the gender-identity reading, or is genetic fallacy? Authority grounding may be contested on historical grounds.
omegas.source: Extraction anchors; historical development section; potential F34 (epistemic trespass into history of psychology)
